prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop landing-page direction comp for TomorrowWorks
Primary request: Render the first viewport and start of the next section of a public Malaysian career guidance website, edge to edge, with crisp readable text and no browser frame. The visitor wants to understand where their existing skills can take them.
Real content: brand “TomorrowWorks”; navigation “Explore careers”, “Job market”, “How it works”, “For organisations”; utility “BM / 中文”; headline “Your experience can take you further.”; supporting text “Discover career directions that fit your skills, see what is changing in Malaysia, and build a realistic learning plan.”; working input label “What do you do now?” with value “Accounting assistant”; primary action “Find my direction”; trust line “Malaysian job-market evidence · Recognised skill data · No CV required”. Begin the next section with “See what your experience already opens up”.
Concept: Monsoon Window. One panoramic rain-marked window carries the full viewport as the weather clears from storm ink through rain blue into saffron daylight. The functional skill input sits along the low horizon; three named destination markers—Bookkeeper, Accountant, Data analyst—emerge in the clearing, connected by one sweeping arc. Navigation is embedded cleanly into the upper edge.
Visual law: deep storm blue ground, luminous blue-to-amber horizon, pale daylight, translucent forecast-film labels, contemporary humane sans typography, one dominant horizon move. The page must still read as a working public website, not a poster or weather app.
Constraints: no sidebar, no dashboard, no chatbot, no glassmorphism cards, no generic centred hero, no separate row of equal feature cards, no invented statistics, no fake testimonials, no AI robot imagery, no watermark.
